title: Email Metadata: March 2

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Email Metadata: March 2
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The following metadata for emails sent by all accounts operated by the mayor's office between the dates of March 15, 2026 and April 3, 2026: Sender, Recipient (To, CC, BCC), Date and time sent, Subject. As this is a request for metadata, please do not include the email body in the returned records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse

title: Local PD emails with LexisNexis or PenLink (East Palestine Police Department)

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Local PD emails with LexisNexis or PenLink (East Palestine Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide emails between your department and LexisNexis Risk Solutions or PenLink. Specifically:
1) All emails to/from the following domains: "@LexisNexis.com" or "@LexisNexisRisk.com" or "@lnssi.com" or "@penlink.com"
2) Timeframe: 2/1/2026 through 8/15/2026
3) Include: Emails, attachments, inline images, header information, and links. 
4) Exclude: Duplicates or mass-emails may be de-duplicated to only produce a single example email (the goal of exclusions is to reduce responsive documents and work - if de-duplicating adds more work please skip it)
5) Format: If possible, please include raw .eml, .msg, or other similar electronic files that maintain the integrity of the original email.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

RE: Records Request; Lexis Nexis Emails

Shawn, 

I have sent the available records to the link you provided.

The East Palestine Police Department has no obligation to respond to duplicate requests according to State ex rel. Laborers Internatl. Union of N. Am., Local Union No. 500 v. Summerville, 122 Ohio St.3d 1234, 2009-Ohio-4090 as included below.

When a public office responds to a request, and the requester sends a follow-up letter reiterating a request for essentially the same records, the public office is not required to provide an additional response.   State ex rel. Laborers Internatl. Union of N. Am., Local Union No. 500 v. Summerville, 122 Ohio St.3d 1234, 2009-Ohio-4090

I trust this satisfies your request. Please call Law Director David Powers at 330-482-3356 with any questions or concerns to expedite an informal resolution in this matter.

title: Crime Free Housing and Nuisance Ordinance Information Request

communications.subject: Arizona Public Records Law Request: Crime Free Housing and Nuisance Ordinance Information Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Arizona Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Any and all records from the past two years (July 2021-July 2023) regarding "crime free" housing and nuisance property ordinances that will be referred to as “program” and "ordinance" respectively, in this request but could be known (but not limited to) as “Crime Free Multi-Housing” and "Disorderly Houses" as described in Phoenix's Code of Ordinances Sec. 23-58.

Please provide any and all written records (including but not limited to hard-copy documents, memos, emails, word processor documents, PDF documents, PowerPoint files, images files, video files etc.) regarding the Program and Ordinance including but not limited to:

• any training/presentation materials used in communication, promotions, workshops, seminars, etc

• criminal background checks performed on prospective tenants

• evictions filed by property owners and number of tenants evicted as a result of the program and ordinance

• suspensions or revocation of a residential rental license, against property owners who fail to comply with the requirements of the ordinance or program

• police calls, reports, citations, or arrests, collected by the municipality police department for the purpose of enforcing the ordinance and program

• meeting minutes and correspondence between municipality officials, regarding the implementation and enforcement of the program and ordinance

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jenny Wadhwa

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Smart Device/AI Assisted Police Calls (Los Angeles Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All incident reports, call logs, computer-aided dispatch (CAD) records, and related documentation from January 1, 2020 to the present reflecting calls for service that were identified as, or subsequently determined to be, initiated by a voice-activated device, virtual assistant, or AI-enabled emergency feature, including but not limited to Apple Siri, Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Samsung Bixby, or device-based emergency detection features such as Apple crash detection, fall detection, or Emergency SOS.

All incident reports, call logs, and related documentation from January 1, 2020 to the present reflecting calls for service categorized as accidental, unintentional, pocket dial, abandoned, or device-generated, where responding officers noted or documented that the call originated from a smart device or voice-activated assistant.

Any internal policies, directives, training materials, bulletins, or guidance documents related to responding to or handling calls originating from voice-activated devices, virtual assistants, or AI-enabled emergency features on smart devices.

Any communications, including emails, memos, or internal reports, discussing accidental or unintentional 911 calls generated by AI, smart devices or voice assistants.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

title: Steven Catron (Flora Police Department)

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Steven Catron (Flora Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Steven Catron (6303-1830)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

title: Pete Sumalo Montejo ICE Death Report

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Pete Sumalo Montejo ICE Death Report
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The ICE Detainee Death Report for Pete Sumalo Montejo, who passed away December 5, 2025, in ICE custody in Texas. 
2. A copy of the ICE ERO or IHSC Significant Incident Report or Significant Event Notification

According to the information currently published on ICE's website, ICE was under a Congressional mandate to release this information no later than 30 days after his death, and to update it no more than 60 days after each immigrant's death. ICE has released a Death Report for Jean Wilson Brutus and Shiraz Sachwani, both of whom died after Mr. Sumalo Montejo. 

I make this request under both 5 USC 552(a)(2) - which governs the agency's affirmative disclosure obligations - and 552(a)(3), which concerns the agency's obligation to respond to a request. 

Pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e)(1)(ii) and (iv), I seek expedited processing of this request, and certify and attest under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and current understanding: 

1. I am a member of the media, primarily engaged information dissemination. See www.MuckRack.com/Andrew-Free.

2. I research and publish regarding deaths in ICE custody. My work documenting deaths in ICE detention is published, cited, and relied upon by national media outlets, including the Washington Post, the New York Times, the L.A. Times, and others. 

3. As of the date of filing my filing of this request, ICE has not posted its Detainee Death Report for this individual. 

4. There is an urgent need to inform the public about the circumstances ICE is aware of surrounding this death. Congress is currently contemplating alterations to DHS and ICE's funding, and the facts of each death in custody directly impact demands lawmakers and the public may wish to press when authorizing future funding increases, or applying limits to them.

5. Deaths in ICE custody reached their highest numbers in 20 years in 2025, and they have been the subject of widespread media coverage, and there is significant reason to believe ICE's treatment of people in detention has not met the standards it claims it adheres to when defending its actions in public statements. This coverage has prompted a number of responses by DHS's Twitter page and other public statements, pushing back against the coverage.

6. I will make the records available to the general public upon receiving them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: ICE FOIA 2026-ICFO-16837
communications.communication:
06/09/2026 

Andrew  Free 
MuckRock News, DEPT MR204566 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2026-ICFO-16837 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 2/11/2026, and to your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 2/11/2026. Specifically, you requested records for Pete Sumalo Montejo. 

Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 

Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 

Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).   You have not established that lack of expedited treatment in this case will pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual.  While you may be primarily engaged in the dissemination of information, you have not detailed with specificity why you feel there is an urgency to inform the public about Pete Sumalo Montejo.  Qualifying urgency would need to exceed the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  You also did not offer sufficient supporting evidence of an interest of the public greater than the public’s general interest in Pete Sumalo Montejo.  Your letter was conclusory in nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10- day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you care to narrow the scope of your request, please contact our office. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request.  We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations, as they apply to media requesters.  As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free.  We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically through the SecureRelease Portal (preferred) or via regular mail to: 

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Office of the Principal Legal Advisor 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
500 12th Street,, S.W., Mail Stop 5900 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5900 

Your envelope and letter should be marked “FOIA Appeal.”  Copies of the FOIA and DHS regulations are available at www.dhs.gov/foia. 

ICE has queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, please contact the FOIA office or FOIA Public Liaison at ICEFOIAPublicLiaison@ice.dhs.gov or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned tracking number 2026-ICFO-16837. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

communications.subject: FW: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Administrative Processing, Electronic Case-Management Records DeKalb County Superior Court
communications.communication:
Good Afternoon Mr. DeLozier:

Thank you for your request to view DeKalb County Superior Court Clerk’s Office records pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71. Our office received your below request on September 21, 2026. While requests for government documents in Georgia are frequently submitted pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq.), it is well-established under Georgia law that the Open Records Act does not apply to the judicial branch of government or the offices of court clerks.
Instead, public access to court records is strictly governed by Rule 21 of the Georgia Uniform Superior Court Rules (USCR). USCR Rule 21 explicitly mandates a broad presumption of openness.

In that vein, you may access court records via the following links:

https://portal-gadekalb.tylertech.cloud/portal
https://deeds.dekalbcountyga.gov/LandmarkWeb
https://www.gsccca.org/
https://efilega.tylertech.cloud<https://efilega.tylertech.cloud/>

You may also inspect court records in our office located at 556 N. McDonough Street, Ground Floor, Decatur, Georgia 30030 between the hours of 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM). Finally, attached hereto are the Civil Division Complete Manual and the Mandatory E-file Order that is responsive to your request.

Please do not hesitate to contact me should you have any questions or concerns related to this matter.

Sincerely,

Xernia

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: DPD pilot ALPR Program Documents
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Denver Police Department installed an LPR system as a pilot program at the intersection of 6th and Federal on Oct 19, 2018. It was reported to cost ~$62,000.
In communicating with DPD, I was informed the system’s camera units were Federal Signal, then bought by 3M, then bought by Neology. I am not sure if any of those brands were the vendor.

- Facebook post by DPD, saying "we just added a stationary system at 6th Avenue and Federal Boulevard. We began employing this LPR on October 19th, 2018." 
(https://www.facebook.com/denverpolice/posts/1640540512717592/)
- Article by The Denver Post which mentions "The new installation on Federal cost $62,000" listing their source as "police spokesperson Christine Downs."
(https://www.denverpost.com/2018/10/09/denver-police-license-plate-camera-scan-federal-boulevard/)
- Article from Denver7 which quotes Division Chief (at the time) Ron Thomas: "'That’s a location that we’ve identified through data. We’ve got a lot of stolen vehicles in that area. We’ve had a lot of hit-and-runs at that particular intersection so our data just suggested that would be the best location,' said Division Chief Ron Thomas."
(https://www.denver7.com/news/local-news/denver-police-will-scan-every-license-plate-at-federal-blvd-and-6th-ave)

I filed records request with Denver Department of Safety and they referred me to the Office of the Clerk and Recorder for the records, claiming C&R is the official custodian of the records.

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

- A list of DPD's contracts and receipts from Jan 1, 2017 - Dec 31st, 2018 for cameras, digital recording equipment and image recognition software.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

title: Flock Audit Logs Dunwoody October - December 2024

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Audit Logs Dunwoody October - December 2024
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all audit logs, search logs, or usage reports related to your agency's use of Flock "ALPR" systems for the period October 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024. This includes but is not limited to the "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit" logs available in the Flock software's "Insights" section, showing records of license plate searches performed by agency personnel, timestamps of searches, user identification information (names, badge numbers, or user IDs), and any associated case numbers or investigation references.

Please provide records in their original electronic format (CSV, Excel, or similar).

To the extent any portion of these records is claimed exempt under the Open Records Act, I request that the exemption be applied at the field or column level rather than by withholding entire logs, consistent with the segregability requirement of O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A). If a specific field (such as the free-text search justification field) is withheld, please identify which field and the specific statutory basis for withholding it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: Paper Trails & Precipices: How Ward 8 Residents are Exposing D.C.'s Stormwater Cover-Up
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov, sharon.kershbaum@dc.gov, earl.eutsler@dc.gov, duff.mccully@dc.gov

CC: hq.foia@epa.gov, r3public@epa.gov, oig_hotline@epa.gov, enrd.mail@usdoj.gov, rwhite@dccouncil.gov, swilson@dccouncil.gov, pmendelson@dccouncil.us, callen@dccouncil.gov, twhite@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com, tkopania@wusa9.com, lajoy.johnson-law@dc.gov
Subject: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: UFD Work Orders, GPS Telemetry, & Native Audit Logs (1488-1500 Morris Rd SE) - Sept 9, 2026

To the District Department of Transportation FOIA Officer and Executive Leadership:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-532), I am formally demanding the immediate release of the following public records pertaining to the Urban Forestry Division (UFD) work order and crew deployment that occurred today, September 9, 2026, within the 1488 to 1500 block of Morris Rd SE.

This request specifically encompasses, but is not limited to, the following mandatory disclosures:

1. Unredacted Work Orders & Native Metadata:
The complete, unredacted Service Request (SR) files, dispatch tickets, and UFD Work Orders generated for 1488, 1490, and 1500 Morris Rd SE for operations scheduled between 7:00 AM and 3:00 PM on September 9, 2026. This must be provided in its native digital format to preserve all embedded metadata.

2. Comprehensive Audit Logs & Change History:
The complete digital "Audit Log" and "Change History" for the aforementioned tickets from your internal asset management system. This must include every status change, exact timestamp, dispatcher comment, field-crew upload, and the Employee ID/Name of any individual who modified, placed on hold, or escalated the ticket at any point today.

3. AVL / GPS Telemetry Data:
The exact Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) GPS telemetry data and physical coordinates for all DDOT/UFD vehicles, bucket trucks, and crew members dispatched to the 1400-1600 block of Morris Rd SE on September 9, 2026. This data must reflect their exact arrival times, movement within the public right-of-way, and departure times to confirm municipal presence adjacent to the active landslide.

4. Vaughn Index Directive:
Let this serve as formal notice: If DDOT attempts to redact any internal notes, executive directives, or dispatcher comments under the guise of the "Deliberative Process Privilege" (D.C. Official Code § 2-534), you are legally required to produce a detailed Vaughn Index. This index must specifically describe each redacted record, state the exact statutory exemption claimed, and explain precisely why the disclosure of a routine tree-maintenance ticket would harm agency decision-making. 

As a community advocate monitoring an active 25-foot landslide and federal MS4 compliance failure, I expect strict adherence to the statutory deadlines governing this demand.

​5. FEE WAIVER REQUEST:
Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees. Disclosure of this information is in the primary public interest to inform District residents and investigative media at WUSA9 regarding municipal compliance with public space and infrastructure management in Ward 8. The requester is a community advocate with zero commercial interest in these materials.

Notice of External Tracking: Please be advised that this FOIA request, its processing timeline, and your ultimate response is being simultaneously monitored by WUSA-9 investigative reporters and investigative journalists as part of an ongoing inquiry into systemic municipal infrastructure neglect.

https://youtu.be/9-FMo6HNbfA?si=73RawTp5o5C83go_

"Ward 8 Excellence: Do the Work. Protect YOUR people. No Exceptions." Govern yourselves accordingly.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

Thank you for your interest in public records of District of Columbia. Your request has been received and is being processed. Your request was received in this office on 9/10/2026 and given the reference number R013981-091026 for tracking purposes. 
In all future correspondence regarding this request, please reference request number R013981-091026. You can monitor the progress of your request in the " My Records Center". 
 
The District of Columbia is required to respond to your FOIA request within fifteen (15) business days of its receipt.  See D.C. Official Code § 2-532(c)(2011).  However, under certain circumstances, D.C. Official Code § 2-532(d)(2011) authorizes the District to extend, by ten (10) additional days, the deadline by which it must respond to a FOIA request.  One of the circumstances provided by that statute is a case in which the District needs additional time to search for, collect and examine voluminous amounts of records and/or consult with an additional D.C. agency. 
For any questions regarding your request, please contact the FOIA office directly. Find the list of agency Open Government and FOIA contact information by visiting FOIA Contact Information. For ease of reference, we ask that you have your FOIA Reference Number available when you contact the FOIA office. 
Regards, 
District of Columbia

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Community ALPR Audit (Tazewell County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

I hereby request the following records: 1. Justification Records All records used to justify adoption of Flock Safety cameras, including but not limited to: staff reports, city council or county board memoranda, crime analysis reports, presentations, vendor proposals, and any other documents that described the purpose, anticipated benefit, or stated rationale for purchasing or leasing the system. 
2. Effectiveness and Use Statistics All statistical reports, internal summaries, use-justification documents, crime-reduction assessments, or after-action reviews evaluating the effectiveness of Flock Safety cameras since installation. This includes any records prepared in connection with contract renewals. 
3. Cost and Financial Records All financial records related to Flock Safety cameras, including invoices, purchase orders, annual subscription payments, installation costs, and maintenance costs from the date of first installation through the present. Include any records showing federal, state, grant, or civil asset forfeiture funding used to offset costs. 
4. Camera Inventory and Placement The current inventory or deployment list of Flock Safety cameras operated by or accessible to this agency, including number of units and general location descriptions. Also include any written policies, criteria, risk assessments, or internal documents used to determine camera placement locations. 
5. Contracts and Legal Agreements Copies of all active and recently expired contracts, amendments, renewals, data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, and scope-of-work documents between this agency and Flock Safety. 
6. Data Access and Network Sharing (a) The Flock "Organization Audit" report showing all searches made within this agency's Flock system from the date of installation through the date of this request. (b) The Flock "Network Audit" report showing all searches of this agency's Flock data by any outside agency from the date of installation through the date of this request. (c) A list of all agencies currently authorized to access this agency's Flock data, including any federal agencies. Please provide these records in their original electronic, machine-readable format (CSV or spreadsheet). 
7. Security Incidents and Unauthorized Access All records documenting any security incidents, unauthorized access, data breaches, hacking events, or unauthorized sharing of data collected by Flock Safety cameras, including any correspondence with or notifications from Flock Safety related to such incidents. 
8. Secretary of State Audit All records, correspondence, or internal communications related to the Illinois Secretary of State's 2025 audit of ALPR data-sharing practices, including any communications with the Secretary of State's office or Flock Safety regarding compliance. 
9. Marketing and Sales Materials All promotional, descriptive, and marketing materials shared with this agency by Flock Safety or any representative thereof prior to or in connection with the purchase or renewal of the Flock Safety system. 
10. Communications with Flock Safety Emails to/from Flock Safety personnel addresses; sales@flocksafety.com, support@flocksafety.com, or any email addresses in the format firstname.lastname@flocksafety.com from January 1, 2022 through the date this request is processed. If this date range is too burdensome due to the amount of emails, then I'd like it narrowed down to January 1, 2022 through December 31, 2022 & January 1, 2025 to the date this request is processed. 
The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

communications.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL]  RE: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Community ALPR Audit (Tazewell County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Requester:
The Tazewell County Sheriff’s Office is pleased to announce that, effective at 12:00 a.m. on September 5, 2026, we will begin using GovQuest as our new online public-records request and delivery system.
GovQuest will provide requesters with a more convenient and transparent way to:

  *   Submit new Freedom of Information Act requests electronically;
  *   Track the status of pending requests;
  *   Receive notifications when a request is being processed, clarification is needed, or a response has been completed;
  *   View released records in one centralized location; and
  *   View and download released video footage through a secure electronic link instead of receiving a disc by mail or arranging an in-person pickup.

No Action Is Required for Your Pending Request
The Sheriff’s Office will manually transfer all currently pending FOIA requests into GovQuest. You do not need to resubmit your request.
Transferring your request will not change its original date of receipt, scope, or current processing status, and it will not restart or extend any applicable response period. After the transfer, you may receive an automated email from GovQuest confirming that your request has been added to the system. This does not represent a new or duplicate request.
Unless a GovQuest notification specifically asks you to provide clarification or additional information, no response or other action is necessary.
GovQuest Accounts and Notifications
Creating a GovQuest account is not required. However, registration is encouraged because an account allows you to log in, view all your requests in one place, and monitor their current status.
When records are released, GovQuest will send an email notification. Links provided for released video footage will allow the footage to be viewed and downloaded electronically. These links will expire after 72 hours, so requesters should download any records they wish to retain before the link expires.
Submitting Future FOIA Requests
Beginning September 5, 2026, GovQuest will be the Sheriff’s Office’s preferred method for submitting FOIA requests electronically:
Submit or Track a FOIA Request Through GovQuest<https://records.govquest.com/tazewellcountysoil/publicportal>
^Click the link above
When submitting an electronic request, please include the complete description of the records requested directly within the GovQuest request fields.
The email address FOIASheriff@tazewell-il.gov<mailto:FOIASheriff@tazewell-il.gov> will no longer be used to receive or process FOIA requests. An automatic response will direct anyone emailing that address to the GovQuest portal.
Use of GovQuest is encouraged but is not required. Written FOIA requests will continue to be accepted by mail or personal delivery at:
Tazewell County Sheriff’s Office
Attn: FOIA Officer
101 S. Capitol Street
Pekin, Illinois 61554
No particular form is required for requests submitted by mail or personal delivery.
This email is an administrative transition notice only. It is not a response, denial, extension, or other determination concerning any pending FOIA request. To avoid duplicate submissions and unnecessary delays, please do not resubmit an existing request or reply solely to confirm receipt of this notice. Once your request is transferred, routine status information will be available through GovQuest.
If you are unable to access the GovQuest portal and require assistance, you may contact the Sheriff’s Office at (309) 477-2250.
Thank you for your cooperation as we make this transition.

Thank you,

FOIA Officer
Tazewell County Sheriff’s Office
101 S. Capitol St., Pekin, IL 61554
foiasheriff@tazewell-il.gov

communications.subject: Request Response Sent - F-RO-26-GQ-000022
communications.communication:
"FOIA Response – Flock Safety / ALPR Records
Dear Mr. Flahaut:
This correspondence is in response to your request under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 ILCS 140/1 et seq.) seeking numerous categories of records concerning the Tazewell County Sheriff's Office's acquisition, use, administration, operation, financing, and oversight of Flock Safety automatic license plate reader (ALPR) technology.
The Sheriff's Office has reviewed your request. As presently written, the request encompasses ten broad categories and numerous subcategories of records, including requests for records extending from the implementation of the Flock Safety system through the present; all system searches and audit activity; communications spanning multiple years; financial, contractual, technical, operational, deployment, security, and administrative records; and records potentially maintained across multiple systems, accounts, divisions, and storage locations.
Request to Reduce Scope – 5 ILCS 140/3(g)
Section 3(g) of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (5 ILCS 140/3(g)) provides that requests calling for all records falling within a category shall be complied with unless compliance with the request as stated would be unduly burdensome, there is no reasonable way to narrow the request, and the burden on the public body outweighs the public interest in the requested information.
Before denying a request as unduly burdensome, Section 3(g) requires a public body to extend to the requester an opportunity to confer in an attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions.
As presently written, processing your request would require the Sheriff's Office to identify, locate, collect, review, and, where necessary, redact a substantial volume of records maintained across multiple systems, accounts, record categories, personnel, and storage locations over a period extending several years. Each potentially responsive record would additionally require individual review to determine whether it contains information exempt from disclosure under FOIA or otherwise prohibited from public disclosure by State or federal law.
Accordingly, pursuant to Section 3(g), the Tazewell County Sheriff's Office is providing you with an opportunity to reduce the request to manageable proportions. Please identify the specific record categories, subject matters, and/or more limited time periods that are of primary interest to you so that the Sheriff's Office may determine whether the request can be processed without imposing an undue burden upon the operations of this public body.
Please be advised that narrowing the scope of the request will not necessarily result in disclosure of all records within the narrowed scope. Certain categories of information identified in your request are independently exempt from disclosure as explained below.
Flock Safety / ALPR Information – 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(d-7)
Section 7(1)(d-7) of FOIA (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(d-7)) exempts from disclosure information gathered or records created from the use of automatic license plate readers in connection with Section 2-130 of the Illinois Vehicle Code.
Section 2-130(d) of the Illinois Vehicle Code (625 ILCS 5/2-130(d)) further provides that ALPR information shall be held confidentially to the fullest extent permitted by law.
Accordingly, to the extent your request seeks Flock Safety or other ALPR-generated information, including search activity, search histories, audit records reflecting ALPR searches, plate-hit information, search targets, search results, images, historical-location information, maps, timelines, travel-pattern information, data-sharing activity, or other information gathered or records created through the use or analysis of ALPR technology, such information is exempt from disclosure pursuant to Section 7(1)(d-7).
This exemption applies to ALPR-derived information contained within or reproduced in another responsive record as well as records generated directly by the ALPR system.
Accordingly, portions of Item 6 of your request seeking the Flock "Organization Audit" and "Network Audit," to the extent those records identify, disclose, or constitute ALPR searches or information gathered or created through the use of ALPR technology, are exempt from disclosure under Section 7(1)(d-7).
LEADS Information – 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a)
To the extent responsive records contain information derived from or maintained within the Law Enforcement Agencies Data System (LEADS), such information is exempt from disclosure under Section 7(1)(a) of FOIA (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(a)).
Section 7(1)(a) exempts information specifically prohibited from disclosure by federal or State law or by rules and regulations implementing federal or State law. LEADS data is subject to restricted access and dissemination requirements and is not available for disclosure to the general public.
Accordingly, any protected LEADS information contained within otherwise responsive records will be withheld or redacted as required by law.
Investigative Techniques and Operational Information – 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(d)(v)
Section 7(1)(d)(v) of FOIA (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(d)(v)) permits the withholding of law-enforcement records where disclosure would reveal unique or specialized investigative techniques, other than techniques generally used and known, and disclosure would result in demonstrable harm to the public body.
To the extent responsive records reveal nonpublic operational details concerning how the Sheriff's Office utilizes ALPR technology as an investigative tool, including specific search methodologies, analytical methods, investigative workflows, deployment criteria, or other specialized techniques, those portions will be reviewed for exemption under Section 7(1)(d)(v).
Disclosure of such information could enable individuals to anticipate, avoid, defeat, or circumvent law-enforcement investigative methods and could impair the Sheriff's Office's ability to effectively utilize those methods in future investigations.
This exemption will not be applied merely because a record references Flock Safety or ALPR technology. Rather, it will be applied only where disclosure would reveal a qualifying specialized investigative technique and result in the demonstrable harm contemplated by Section 7(1)(d)(v).
Information Technology and System Security – 5 ILCS 140/7(1)(o)
Section 7(1)(o) of FOIA (5 ILCS 140/7(1)(o)) exempts administrative or technical information associated with automated data-processing operations where disclosure would jeopardize the security of the system, its data, or other exempt information.
Accordingly, responsive records containing nonpublic information concerning system architecture, access controls, authentication methods, account or credential information, security configurations, internal technical operations, vulnerabilities, network-security information, or other technical information whose disclosure could compromise the security or integrity of the system or its data will be withheld or redacted pursuant to Section 7(1)(o), as applicable.
This exemption may be relevant to portions of your request concerning security incidents, unauthorized access, system administration, technical audit information, or other records containing protected information-technology or cybersecurity information.
Camera Inventory and Placement Information
The Sheriff's Office will separately review any responsive records concerning the number, deployment, or placement of Flock Safety cameras.
The fact that a record identifies or discusses the Flock Safety system does not, by itself, render the record exempt. However, specific location, deployment, operational, or technical information will be withheld or redacted where disclosure would reveal exempt ALPR information, specialized investigative techniques, security-sensitive information, or other information protected under FOIA.
Contracts, Financial Records, Policies, and Other Administrative Records
The Sheriff's Office is not asserting that all records concerning Flock Safety are categorically exempt from public disclosure.
Contracts, amendments, invoices, purchase orders, financial records, general policies, vendor materials, administrative correspondence, and similar records will be evaluated independently under FOIA. To the extent such records are responsive and are not otherwise exempt, reasonably segregable nonexempt portions will be produced.
Records containing both exempt and nonexempt information will be redacted as permitted by law rather than withheld in their entirety when reasonably segregable information can be disclosed.
Communications With Flock Safety
Your request seeks communications with Flock Safety personnel from January 1, 2022, through the date of processing, with an alternative date range if the broader search is burdensome.
This portion of the request potentially requires searches across multiple employee accounts and a substantial volume of communications spanning several years. Accordingly, this portion is included within the Sheriff's Office's request under Section 3(g) that you reduce the request to manageable proportions.
Any responsive communications ultimately located will additionally be reviewed for information exempt under Sections 7(1)(d-7), 7(1)(d)(v), 7(1)(o), or other applicable provisions of FOIA.
Existing Records Only
FOIA requires the production of existing public records maintained by or under the custody or control of a public body. The Act does not require the Sheriff's Office to create a new record, prepare a new compilation or analysis, reconstruct historical system activity, or generate a customized report that does not otherwise exist.
Accordingly, the Sheriff's Office will search for and evaluate existing records responsive to any appropriately narrowed request. The Sheriff's Office is not required to create new records or reports solely to satisfy the requested format or informational fields.
Segregation of Nonexempt Information
The Sheriff's Office will review responsive records for reasonably segregable nonexempt information. Where a record contains both exempt and nonexempt information, exempt portions will be withheld or redacted and reasonably segregable nonexempt portions will be disclosed as required by FOIA.
The exemptions identified above are not intended to suggest that each exemption applies to every responsive record. Each responsive record or category of records will be evaluated according to its contents and the applicable provisions of law.
Please provide your proposed narrowed scope so that the Sheriff's Office may proceed with processing your request in accordance with the Illinois Freedom of Information Act.
If you believe this response is in error, you may, in accordance with Section 9 of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (5 ILCS 140/9), seek review by the Public Access Counselor, Office of the Illinois Attorney General, 500 South 2nd Street, Springfield, Illinois 62701; telephone: 877-299-3642; fax: 217-782-1396; email: Public.Access@ilag.gov.
You may also seek judicial review pursuant to Section 11 of the Illinois Freedom of Information Act (5 ILCS 140/11).
Sincerely,
FOIA Officer
Tazewell County Sheriff's Office"

"01/05/2023

Andrew Free
MuckRock News, DEPT MR138127
Boston, Massachusetts 02115

RE: ICE FOIA Case Number 2023-ICFO-07524

Dear Requester:

This acknowledges receipt of your 12/20/2022, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), for all records released by ICE to the requester in the request assigned tracking number 2018-ICLI-00052.. Your request was received in this office on 12/20/2022.

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner.

Provisions of the FOIA allow us to recover part of the cost of complying with your request. We shall charge you for records in accordance with the DHS Interim FOIA regulations, as they apply to media requesters. As a media requester, you will be charged 10 cents per page for duplication; the first 100 pages are free. We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued.

We have queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request.

If you have any questions, please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Marcus Francis at the address above or (866) 633-1182. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation. If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974. You may contact OGIS as follows: Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448; or facsimile at 202-741-5769.

Your request has been assigned reference number 2023-ICFO-07524. Please use this number in future correspondence.



Sincerely,

ICE FOIA Office
Immigration and Customs Enforcement
Freedom of Information Act Office
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009"

title: Charlie Kirk Assassination - South Carolina Attorney General

communications.subject: South Carolina Public Records Law Request: Charlie Kirk Assassination - South Carolina Attorney General
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any COMMUNICATIONS (defined below) between the Office of the Attorney General (including, but not limited to, any member of the AG STAFF identified below) and any the leadership of any institution of higher education (whether public or private, and including the institution's president, vice-president, general counsel, public relations personnel, and government relations personnel) concerning remarks, comments, posts, or other communications by a faculty member, staff member, or student. This request is limited to COMMUNICATIONS sent or received on or after September 10, 2025.

2. Any COMMUNICATIONS to or from any of the AG STAFF containing any of the following terms: "Kirk", "TPUSA", "Turning Point", "Clemson", "University of South Carolina", "First Amendment", "academic freedom", "free speech", "freedom of speech", "16-17-560", "political firing". This request is limited to COMMUNICATIONS sent or received on or after September 10, 2025.

3. Any COMMUNICATIONS to or from any of the AG STAFF from (or to) an email address with a .edu domain. This request is limited to COMMUNICATIONS sent or received on or after September 10, 2025.

"COMMUNICATIONS" means and includes emails, text messages, social media messages, letters, memoranda, calendar entries, chats, or any other form of one-to-one or one-to-many communication.

"AG STAFF" means and includes Attorney General Alan Wilson and Whitney Michael.

Please note that this request seeks public records wherever they may be found, including on devices or networks owned or operated by private parties. For example, if an employee uses a personal cell phone or social media account to conduct public business, records created, maintained, or held on the phone or account are public records subject to this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Adam Steinbaugh

title: Burleigh County Jury Summons List Request

communications.subject: North Dakota Open Records Law Request: Burleigh County Jury Summons List Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The following materials regarding the compilation and composition of the state’s master jury list:

All reports, databases, spreadsheets, or equivalent materials regarding the jury summons process. Please include the total number of individuals who were summoned, responded, and who were selected to a jury summons.

In the event that there are any fees for obtaining or copying these records, please inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Should the fees exceed $100, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees as I am requesting the information on behalf of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and the disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest and will contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of how master jury lists are created. This information is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If possible, please provide the requested documents electronically. However, if this is not feasible, please inform me of the available methods for obtaining these records. Further, if you expect a significant delay in responding to this request, please contact me with information concerning when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption that justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within the timeframe required by the statute.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Angel Carter

title: The "Discussed Ditch" Cover-Up: Exposing DC's 25-Foot Ward 8 Landslide

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: The "Discussed Ditch" Cover-Up: Exposing DC's 25-Foot Ward 8 Landslide
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov
CC: eugene.adams@dc.gov; molc.mayor@dc.gov; foia.appeals@dc.gov; tnorflis@dccouncil.gov; rmckinney@dccouncil.gov
Subject: FOIA Request: DDOT Arborist Inspection Logs, Unannounced Site Visits, & Cross-Agency Referrals (1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officer:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am formally requesting copies of the following public records pertaining to the property and public right-of-way located at 1490 Morris Rd SE, Washington, DC 20020. This request includes, but is not limited to, records tied to 311 Service Request #26-00495403, as well as any internally directed, unscheduled, or ad-hoc site visits. 

Please provide the following records generated between August 19, 2026, and today's date, September 2, 2026:

1. All internal arborist inspection notes, field reports, work orders, and photographs taken by DDOT Urban Forestry Division (UFD) personnel or contractors during any physical site visit to 1490 Morris Rd SE (including visits allegedly conducted for "tree trimming" or visual assessment).
2. All internal DDOT email communications, dispatch logs, GPS telematics, and routing metadata discussing the condition of the trees, the soil, the slope, or the authorization of a site visit to this location.
3. All cross-agency referrals, notifications, or memoranda sent by DDOT personnel to the Department of Buildings (DOB), the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE), or the Office of Unified Communications (OUC) regarding the 25-foot slope failure/landslide observed at this location. 

Because the DDOT Urban Forestry Division physically assessed the property but lacks the geotechnical jurisdiction to abate a 25-foot structural landslide, the internal referrals transferring this life-safety hazard to the appropriate structural authorities (DOB/DOEE) are highly relevant to public safety and current oversight investigations.

I request these records be produced in their native electronic format. I am requesting a fee waiver as this request is in the public interest and is actively contributing to public understanding of District infrastructure and hazard response protocols in Ward 8.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

Thank you for submitting a request for records on 08/17/2026. Your request has been received and is being processed. Please be advised that if your request was submitted after 4:30 PM, during the weekend, or on a County holiday, it will be received and processed the following business day. 
  
 Your request reference number is Request Number: RTK-453-2026 and your security key is 71930531. 
  
 Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: Subject: STATE CONSTABLE GLENN MARKLEY Records Request - Constable Vendor Financial Records & Audit Trail Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right-to-Know Law (65 P.S. § 67.101 et seq.), I hereby request copies of specific financial records documenting the expenditure of public funds to the constable vendor identified below; About Samuel Glenn Markley (aka GLENN MARKLEY) or any PERSON he uses (e.g. INCARCERATE INC, "0000033488 Incarcerate, Inc.") provide specific financial records for periods of dates including: A. April 9th of 2024 through May 14th of 2024, B. June 18th of 2024 through August 6th of 2024, C. September 23rd of 2025 through November 18th of 2025, D. January 27th of 2026 through April 11th of 2026; This request is strictly for fiscal and administrative records held by the Chester County Controller’s Office regarding vendor payment processing, auditing, and disbursement; these records constitute "financial records" and "expenditure reports" under Section 102 of the RTKL; judicial case files, court opinions, investigative notes, or records protected by Pa.R.J.A. No. 509 are not being requested at this time; to the extent any document contains sensitive personal information, this request includes that only defendant names be redacted, while docket numbers, fees, dates, and service descriptions remain visible as they are essential financial line-item descriptors;;; Specific Records Requested: This request is for electronic copies (PDF) of the following documents, using the exact titles as they appear in the Chester County Constable Handbook and Controller’s Office records: A. Original Executed Payment Sheets (Invoices): 1. all Criminal Payment Sheets and Civil Payment Sheets submitted by the named constable during the dates, 2. all Children, Youth and Families Payment Forms and Juvenile Transport Payment Sheets, 3. requirement includes that these records must be the original executed copies containing both the Constable’s signature and the Magisterial District Judge’s (MDJ) signature in the Verification section—do not provide unsigned drafts, data exports, or summaries; B. Recapitulation Sheets: all Criminal Recapitulation Sheets and Civil Recapitulation Sheets submitted by the constable to group the above Payment Sheets; C. Server Fee Notices: all Server Fee Notices (Treasurer’s Copies) associated with the requested Payment Sheets, showing the fees assessed by the court; D. Internal Accounts Payable Vouchers: all Accounts Payable Vouchers created by the Controller’s Office corresponding to each approved Payment Sheet, showing the assigned Voucher Number, general ledger codes, and approved amount; E. Payment Registers and Check Logs: the specific pages from the Check Register or Payment Log showing the Check Numbers (or EFT Trace Numbers), Payment Dates, Vendor Payment ID, and the specific list of Voucher Numbers consolidated into each payment; F. Canceled Checks / EFT Confirmations: images of the front and back of all Canceled Checks or electronic transfer confirmations issued to this vendor for the requested dates; G. Audit and Adjustment Documentation: any internal memos, emails, Audit Correction Notes, or correspondence between the Controller’s Office, the Constable, or the MDJ regarding adjustments, reductions, denials, or queries about the requested Payment Sheets;;; Format And Redaction Instructions: A. Format—this request is for these records in electronic format (PDF), if records exist only in paper format, provide written instructions on how to inspect and copy them at your office; B. Do Not Redact: Docket Numbers, Case Numbers, Dates of Service, Type of Service, Mileage Claims, Fees Charged, Vendor Name, or Signatures—these are essential financial data points required to audit the expenditure of public funds; C. May Redact: Defendant Names and Plaintiff Names (if strictly required for privacy), provided the Docket Number remains visible to allow cross-referencing with public court records; D. Per Office of Open Records precedent, docket numbers on financial invoices are public financial descriptors, not confidential judicial deliberations—redacting them prevents the public from verifying if the billed service corresponds to a public court record, violating the core purpose of the RTKL;;; The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: ddot.foia@dc.gov; ouc.foia@dc.gov

CC: callen@dccouncil.gov; pmendelson@dccouncil.us; twhite@dccouncil.gov; ian.maggard@dc.gov; frank.seales@dc.gov; earl.eutsler@dc.gov; david.dickman@dc.gov; ldonovan@wusa9.com; chernande1@wusa9.com

Subject: FOIA REQUEST: 311 Service Request #26-00495403, Urban Forestry Site Metadata, and Imminent Danger Exception (1600-1490 Morris Rd SE)
To the Designated Freedom of Information Act Officers:

Pursuant to the D.C. Freedom of Information Act, I request all records, inspection logs, arborist notes, photographs, owner notification records, and device logs associated with 311 Service Request #26-00495403. Under D.C. Official Code § 2-532(a-1), I specifically demand that all responsive electronic records—especially digital photographs, GPS tracking data, and field logs—be produced in their native electronic format with all original metadata completely intact and unaltered. 

This request explicitly seeks to verify whether a physical site visit was actually conducted or if the Urban Forestry Division improperly relied on stale documentation to close out an urgent safety hazard. Please provide the full identification of the arborist who handled this request, including their full name, title, badge or employee identification number, and any associated field notes. Furthermore, this request seeks to verify whether the DC Urban Forester fulfilled their statutory duty under District arboricultural regulations to formally notify the property owner on record regarding an active life-safety hazard. The trees in question are actively failing, uprooting, and sliding down the public right-of-way, triggering the mandatory Imminent Danger Exception which requires public safety flagging, barricades, or an emergency abatement order rather than administrative dismissal via a "private property" loophole. 

Additionally, this 311 ticket and its mishandling do not exist in a vacuum; they represent a direct symptom of the larger, systemic municipal infrastructure failure. The structural collapse and severe soil erosion threatening these mature trees result from the complete absence of engineered stormwater management. This water originates at the crest of 1600 Morris Rd SE and flows unchecked down the unimproved paper alley corridor to 2258 Hunter Pl SE. 

Fee Waiver Request: Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I request a full fee waiver for this request. Disclosure of this information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of municipal infrastructure failures, environmental safety hazards, and agency compliance with District law. The requester has no commercial interest in the disclosure of these records and is acting in the capacity of a community advocate and public watchdog.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

CC: pmendelson@dccouncil.gov; callen@dccouncil.gov; trayon.white@dc.gov; richard.jackson2@dc.gov; brian.hanlon@dc.gov; ldonovan@wusa9.com; chernande1@wusa9.com; lmaestas@dcprep.org; kim.jackson@k12.dc.gov; alvin.denmark@k12.dc.gov; kisha.white@k12.dc.gov; oss.supervisors@dc.gov

Subject: D.C. FOIA REQUEST: Expedited - Unredacted Urban Forestry Assessment, Intact Metadata & GPS Telemetry (1490 Morris Rd SE)

To the District Department of Transportation (DDOT) FOIA Officer,

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am formally requesting copies of the following public records:

1. The complete, unredacted field report, assessment, and all preliminary or finalized inspector notes generated from the DDOT Urban Forestry Division site visit to 1490 Morris Road SE conducted on the afternoon of August 17, 2026.
2. All original, unaltered photograph and video files taken during this August 17, 2026 site visit. These files must be provided in their native digital formats (e.g., raw JPEG, HEIC) with all original EXIF data and metadata fully intact, including timestamps, GPS coordinates, and camera orientation.
3. All internal communications (including emails, text messages, and direct messages) between the assigned urban forester, Earl Eutsler, Director Sharon Kershbaum, the other two unnamed urban foresters, and any other DDOT staff regarding the findings of this specific site visit.
4. All GPS telemetry data, Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) tracking logs, and routing records for the government-issued vehicle assigned to the responding urban forester on August 17, 2026.
5. All call logs, SMS transmission records, and location data associated with the government-issued cellular device used by the responding urban forester on August 17, 2026.

The glaring omission of the 75-year-old Heritage White Oak and the active landslide from the provided photographs raises serious questions about the legitimacy, scope, and duration of yesterday's purported site visit. Obtaining the forester's GPS vehicle telemetry and government-issued cellular data will definitively confirm exactly how much time was actually spent on-site, what exact perimeter was walked, and whether a comprehensive inspection of this imminent life-safety hazard was genuinely conducted—or if this was merely a brief "drive-by" assessment designed to deflect liability and quickly close a ticket.

FEE WAIVER REQUEST: 
I request a complete waiver of all fees associated with processing this request. The disclosure of this information is in the public interest as it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government regarding an unmitigated, active landslide posing a direct life-safety threat to a documented student pedestrian route. This request is not for commercial purposes.

MANDATORY PRESERVATION AND PUBLICATION NOTICE:
Be advised that I have submitted this request, and will upload all resulting agency disclosures, directly to MuckRock.com. This ensures complete transparency and allows investigative journalists, the D.C. Council, and the public to monitor DDOT's compliance. Any attempt to scrub metadata or withhold raw files will be documented on the public record. 

Given the imminent life-safety threat to the DC Prep student route as the academic year begins today, I request expedited processing. 

Respectfully,

Fred Gamble Jr.
1490 Morris Rd SE
Fort Stanton Neighbors
Washington, DC 20020
(301) 651-8904

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

Public reports state that this county is using cameras from Flock Safety (a.k.a. "Flock"), the automatic license plate reader (ALPR) company. For the purposes of this request, when I refer to "Flock products," this includes hardware (Flock License Plate Readers (LPRs), Flock Safety Falcons, Flock Video Cameras, Flock Mobile Security Trailers, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection Devices, Flock Drone as First Responder (DFRs), and Flock Alpha) as well as software (Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Flock FreeForm, Flock Vehicle Fingerprint technology, and the National LPR Network). Source:
https://www.flocksafety.com/products
Therefore, pursuant to Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records (dated September 19, 2026 to the time this request is processed):
1. All contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, payment records, budgetary quotes, and related procurement records involving Flock Safety.
2. All training, instructional, presentation, and guidance materials concerning the use of any Flock Safety product or service, including hardware and software. This includes, but is not limited to:
a) Presentations, videos, audio recordings, scripts, manuals, and training materials;
b) Meeting notes discussing the use of Flock products;
c) Technical or operational explanations of how Flock products function; and
d) Internal or external documents used to explain, train on, or promote the use of Flock products.
3. All policies, procedures, agreements, and legal documents relating to Flock Safety or its products, including terms and conditions, privacy impact assessments, standard operating procedures, use policies, data retention policies, legal opinions, warranties, nondisclosure agreements, memoranda of understanding, liability waivers, insurance agreements, and any other formal or informal agreements.

4. All audit, oversight, or compliance records relating to Flock Safety or its products, including security audits, misuse investigations, and reports submitted to oversight bodies.
5. All records reflecting requests from other law enforcement agencies or private entities for data obtained through Flock products, including but not limited to requests for LPR data.
6. All communications and documents that reference
"Flock" / "Flock Safety," including emails, text messages, PDFs, word processing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, etc.
7. All communications with representatives of Flock Safety (email domain: @flocksafety.com) and any and all reports and data of your audits you have made as an agency yourself or have been subject to by any flock audits (such as the as publicly reported in the Franklin county Citizen. )

Please try to include any other miscellaneous documents that facilitate this municipality's relationship with Flock that don't neatly fall neatly into the above categories.
